stem: The Provincial Governments were constituted under the Act of-
expl: On the basis of the Government of India Act, 1935, elections to the provincial legislatures were held in February 1937. In these elections, Congress wiped out its rival parties and secured an absolute majority in five provinces—Madras (159 out of 215 seats), Bihar (98 out of 152), Central Provinces and Berar (70 out of 112), United Provinces (134 out of 228), and Orissa (36 out of 60). Congress emerged as the largest party in Bombay (almost an absolute majority), Assam, and the North-West Frontier Province. Only in Bengal, Punjab, and Sind was Congress unable to become the largest party. In July 1937, Congress formed its governments in 6 provinces—Madras, United Provinces, Central Provinces and Berar, Bihar, Bombay, and Orissa. Note: In Bombay, Congress got almost an absolute majority (86 out of 175 seats). In Ayodhya Singh’s book 'Bharat Ka Mukti-Sangram', Congress is shown as having an absolute majority in Bombay as well (88 out of 175 seats), which, according to other sources, is not correct.

stem: Who was elected the President of Indian National Congress in 1938?
expl: At the Haripura (Gujarat) session of the Congress (February 1938), Subhas Chandra Bose was elected President unopposed. It is noteworthy that in 1939, at the Tripuri session, he was elected President by defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

stem: Who become the President of Indian National Congress when Subhash Chandra Bose resigned in 1939?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: At the Haripura (Gujarat) session of the Congress in 1938, Subhas Chandra Bose became Congress President for the first time (unopposed). At the Tripuri session of 1939, he became President for the second time by defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, who was supported by Gandhiji; however, due to differences with Gandhiji on the issue of constituting the Working Committee, he resigned, after which Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the acting President of Congress. During this period (August–September 1945), Clement Attlee was the Prime Minister of Britain, not Churchill. After the change of power in Britain in July 1945, Attlee (1945–1951) became Prime Minister in place of Churchill. In an official research note of the British Parliament (House of Lords Library), it is clearly stated that the confirmation of the end of the Second World War was made through a radio broadcast by Prime Minister Attlee.

stem: The purpose of the Butler Committee, 1927:

options.label: c
options.text: Implementation of Sensor over National Newspapers.

options.label: d
options.text: Improvement of relationships between Indian Provinces and the Crown.

expl: The Butler Committee was constituted in 1927; it is also called the Indian States Committee. Its objective was to examine the relations between the Government of India and the Indian princely states, and to make recommendations to improve the economic and financial relations between British India and the princely states. The Indian rulers appointed a well-known lawyer, Leslie Scott, to present their viewpoint before the Committee. Scott argued that each princely state was originally independent, and therefore it remained independent except to the extent to which it had surrendered its sovereignty to the British Crown; that is, special rights/ privileges lay with the princely states.

stem: All India State People's Conference was set up in –
expl: The All-India States’ People’s Conference was organized in December 1927. It was a federation of political movements and Praja Mandals in the princely states under British rule. About 700 political activists from different princely states participated in it and played an important role in its organization.

stem: Who was the British Prime Minister of Britain during the Second World War?
expl: At the beginning of the Second World War (1939–45), the British Prime Minister was Neville Chamberlain (1937–40), and during the Second World War the British Prime Minister was Winston Churchill (tenure 1940–45). Note—Winston Churchill served as British Prime Minister twice: 1940–45 and 1951–55.

expl: A Cambridge University student, Chaudhry Rahmat Ali, wrote a pamphlet in 1933 titled Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish for Ever? In it, he demanded a separate national status for a new identity, which he named Pakistan. [In his pamphlet, Chaudhry Rahmat Ali used the word ‘Pakstan’ (PAKSTAN), which was later called ‘Pakistan’ (PAKISTAN).] The word “Pakistan” was formed from the first letters of Punjab, Afghan Province, Kashmir and Sindh, and the last three letters of Balochistan— P - Punjab A - Afghan Province (North-West Frontier Province) K - Kashmir S - Sindh Tan - Balochistan

stem: Who raised the cry "Divide and Quit"
expl: The slogan “Divide and Quit” was raised by the Muslim League leader Muhammad Ali Jinnah during the Second World War, in 1943. Jinnah and the Muslim League demanded that the British should first divide India into two parts—Hindustan and Pakistan—and then quit India. This idea was expressed in the form of the political slogan “Divide and Quit”.

stem: Who among following led the movement for the separate State of Pakistan?
expl: On 22–24 March, 1940, the Muslim League session was held at Lahore. It was presided over by Muhammad Ali Jinnah. In this session, a resolution was passed demanding ‘independent states’ for the Muslims of the north-western and eastern regions; this is known as the ‘Lahore Resolution’. Later, this ‘Lahore Resolution’ came to be known as the ‘Pakistan Resolution’. However, it is noteworthy that this resolution mentioned neither partition nor the word ‘Pakistan’. In the Lahore Resolution, it was stated that separate independent states should be formed by grouping together the Muslim-majority regions of north-western and eastern India—not a single independent nation. Some people at that time interpreted it as a demand for two independent countries (India and Pakistan). However, the Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) later paved the way for the creation of Pakistan.

stem: When did Muslim League observe “Direct Action Day” ?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The date 16 August, 1946 was fixed by the Muslim League for “Direct Action Day”. Rejecting the Viceroy’s decision regarding the Interim Government, the Muslim League demanded the establishment of an independent and fully sovereign state of Pakistan. The aim on that date was to incite riots and create an atmosphere of terror to show that Hindus and Muslims could not live together. In this action, Noakhali became a major centre of the riots.

stem: Whom did Rajendra Prasad consider as the father of Pakistan?

expl: Rajendra Prasad regarded Lord Minto as the father of Pakistan. It may be noted that the system of communal representation introduced in the Morley–Minto Reforms of 1909 greatly encouraged communalism, which ultimately led to Partition.
